purpose: Nineteenth expanded public source layer focused on decision provenance, conflicting evidence, scale-up transfer, model uncertainty, robustness/design-of-experiments, benchmark leakage, local route-card validation, and strategic failure-case records. These records capture why a route should be trusted, rejected, quarantined, or manually reviewed beyond ordinary reaction-template feasibility.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, process, data-curation, model-validation, regulatory, safety, and project-owner review

explicit route-choice rationale, source-conflict resolution, scale-up transfer evidence, calibrated model uncertainty, DoE/robustness evidence, leakage-free split lineage, local route-card signoff, or failure-case correction before proposal promotion
separate decision-trace, literature-conflict, tech-transfer, model-uncertainty, robustness, data-leakage, local-source, and failure-case policy

route-specific rejected alternatives, source hierarchy, equipment/site transfer boundary, uncertainty calibration or domain evidence, parameter sensitivity, patent-family or analogue-series split evidence, manually verified structures/stereochemistry, and negative/failure label provenance
safety, legal, copyright, source-license, model-governance, data-governance, regulatory, and project-approval review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid operational quantities, executable procedures, hazardous instructions, assay protocols, scale-up instructions, and unpublished proprietary details

v20 records are source-quality and route-policy priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated process transfers, validated model predictions, validated local route cards, or final failure labels

families.name: Route comparison, rejected-alternative rationale, chemist decision trace, and route-selection provenance policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate the route that was chosen from the decision evidence that made it preferable. A strategic source should preserve rejected alternatives, tradeoffs, objective, cost, availability, risk, and human-review rationale rather than only the winning route.

families.name: Literature, patent, database, yield, structure, and procedure conflict-resolution source-quality policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a reported transformation from the source hierarchy that supports it. Conflicting yields, identities, procedures, patents, extracted records, and database rows need provenance, source tier, extraction confidence, and reviewer resolution before route promotion.

families.name: Scale-up, lab-to-pilot transfer, technology transfer, equipment fit, cleaning, hold-time, and site-transfer boundary policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate bench feasibility from transferability. Route value can change when equipment, site, batch/flow format, cleaning, hold time, raw-material control, and process-knowledge transfer become the controlling constraints.

families.name: Computational prediction uncertainty, calibration, applicability domain, out-of-distribution, and model-evidence route policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a model prediction from its calibrated uncertainty and domain of applicability. Predicted retrosynthesis, conditions, selectivity, toxicity, property, or feasibility records need uncertainty, calibration, OOD, and evidence-bounded confidence before route use.

families.name: Route robustness, design-of-experiments, design space, parameter sensitivity, impurity response, and operating-window policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a route that works once from a route with an evidence-bounded operating window. DoE, robustness, sensitivity, impurity response, design space, and failure-mode evidence can determine whether a source is reliable.

families.name: Analogue-series, scaffold, patent-family, template, benchmark split, and train/test leakage policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate benchmark evidence from source leakage. Analogue-series overlap, shared patent families, template leakage, duplicated structures, source-document overlap, and split lineage must be recorded before using source records for evaluation or model training.

families.name: Local project route-card, PPTX/doc extraction, manual structure/stereochemistry validation, evidence-file, and reviewer-signoff policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate local source extraction from trusted route knowledge. PPTX, slides, rendered schemes, and project docs need manually verified structures, stereochemistry, file provenance, reviewer signoff, and template-promotion status.

families.name: Strategic failure case, non-stock false closure, implausible disconnection, model artifact, and corrected-source policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate route success metrics from failures that teach source policy. False stock closures, product-like terminals, self loops, carrier-reagent misclassification, unsupported atom gains, and corrected labels should become auditable negative source records.

anchors.name: Route-comparison anchor with reviewed objectives, alternatives, rejected-route rationale, cost/risk tradeoffs, and decision provenance
Source-quality anchor with reviewed patent/literature/database conflict, extraction confidence, procedure context, and resolution decision
Scale-up/tech-transfer anchor with reviewed equipment, site, process knowledge, cleaning, hold time, and transfer-risk boundary
Prediction-uncertainty anchor with reviewed calibration, applicability domain, OOD status, prediction interval, and experimental support
Robustness/DoE anchor with reviewed critical parameters, design space, sensitivity, impurity response, and operating-window evidence
Benchmark split/leakage anchor with reviewed analogue-series, scaffold, patent-family, template, source-document, and duplicate lineage
Local route-card anchor with source file, extracted scheme, manually verified structures, stereochemistry, hazards, and reviewer signoff
Failure-case anchor with observed artifact, source-backed correction, negative label, guardrail, and replay/evaluation evidence

disconnections.name: Chosen route to rejected alternatives plus objective, risk, availability, and decision-trace boundary

target_classes: process or medicinal chemistry route comparisons

break_bonds: selected route to rejected-route decision boundary
route score to objective-specific tradeoff boundary
forward_logic: separate a route result from the reasons other routes were rejected
track route objective, comparator routes, material availability, risk, cost, schedule, and reviewer rationale
avoid training or ranking from only the winning route when the rejected alternatives carry strategic information
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward route sources that preserve rejected alternatives and objective-specific tradeoffs instead of only a final route.

evidence.citation: CompRet describes route enumeration and notes that route-evaluation criteria depend on the chemist's situation, objectives, and needs.
Computational planning of complex natural products used expert evaluation to compare computational and human-designed routes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit route objective, rejected alternatives, tradeoff rationale, and reviewer provenance

disconnections.name: Reference route to alternative-route acceptance and non-single-answer evaluation policy

forward_logic: separate reference recall from whether a non-reference route is chemically useful
track route feasibility, stock closure, plausibility, cost, and expert/audit label for alternatives
flag benchmark records that treat one historical route as the only acceptable route
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not penalize non-reference routes by default; require route-quality evidence before accepting or rejecting them.

risks: route metric not aligned with objective

evidence.citation: Predictive chemistry review notes that one-step retrosynthesis evaluation often focuses on recapitulating reported reactants in top-k predictions.
Re-evaluating retrosynthesis algorithms discusses evaluation limits and the difficulty of measuring precision without expert chemists or wet-lab evidence.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit alternative-route audit, stock status, plausibility, and route objective

disconnections.name: Reported transformation to conflicting literature/patent/database evidence plus source-resolution boundary

break_bonds: extracted database row to provenance-resolution boundary
forward_logic: separate a reaction claim from the source hierarchy and conflicts around it
track source type, original document, extraction method, yield/procedure conflicts, identity evidence, and final resolution
avoid promoting a reaction row when patent, paper, database, or extracted procedure evidence disagree
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use reaction-source records only after conflicting source claims are explicitly resolved or quarantined.

evidence.citation: Open Reaction Database schema documentation defines reaction provenance requirements and validation fields.
PatentEye paper reports manual examination of extracted reactions and quantifies extraction accuracy for patent reaction data.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit provenance, conflict type, extraction confidence, and reviewer resolution

disconnections.name: Extracted reaction to LLM/OCR/text-mining confidence, source restoration, and manual-review policy

break_bonds: machine-readable row to original-source restoration boundary
forward_logic: separate machine extraction from a reviewed reaction source
track extraction model/tool, original text or scheme, confidence, false-positive risk, manual correction, and copyright-safe source reference
quarantine rows whose precursor roles, stoichiometry, or product identity cannot be restored to the source
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat extracted reactions as weak sources unless original evidence, confidence, and manual restoration are explicit.

evidence.citation: LLM patent-reaction extraction study evaluates extraction quality and correction of previous false positives.
Automated chemical reaction extraction article describes structured extraction from scientific literature.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit original-source restoration, extraction confidence, manual correction, and role assignment

disconnections.name: Bench route to pilot/manufacturing transfer plus equipment, process-knowledge, and site boundary

break_bonds: process recipe to site-transfer knowledge boundary
forward_logic: separate laboratory feasibility from manufacturing transfer readiness
track scale boundary, equipment fit, process controls, transfer package, site constraints, raw-material controls, and change-control risks
avoid promoting bench sources as scalable routes without transfer evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward scale-up records only when equipment, site, process knowledge, and transfer-risk boundaries are explicit.

evidence.citation: ICH Q10 describes pharmaceutical quality systems across product lifecycle stages including technology transfer and scale-up.
ICH Q11 discusses development and manufacture of drug substances, impurity fate, purification, and process justification.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit scale boundary, transfer package, equipment fit, site constraints, and process control

disconnections.name: Transferred process to cleaning, hold-time, batch/flow format, and lifecycle-control policy

break_bonds: batch or flow mode to lifecycle-control boundary
forward_logic: separate transferred chemistry from operational controls that preserve quality
track cleaning risk, hold-time stability, batch/flow mode changes, containment, in-process controls, and ongoing verification
flag routes where transfer changes residence, storage, contamination, or impurity risk
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use transfer-boundary records when cleaning, hold time, or process format changes route trust.

evidence.citation: ICH Q9(R1) quality risk management guidance frames risk-based decision-making for pharmaceutical quality.
FDA Q10 page describes the ICH Q10 pharmaceutical quality system model and lifecycle implementation.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit cleaning, hold-time, batch/flow comparability, risk assessment, and lifecycle verification

disconnections.name: Predicted route/condition/selectivity to calibrated uncertainty, prediction interval, and applicability-domain boundary

forward_logic: separate a model score from evidence that the score is calibrated for this chemical domain
track model version, training domain, calibration metric, uncertainty interval, OOD status, and experimental support
avoid using high confidence as route evidence when calibration or domain transfer is unknown
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank model-predicted sources outside calibrated domain or without uncertainty evidence.

evidence.citation: JCIM article discusses uncertainty quantification using neural networks for molecular property prediction.
AutoGNNUQ paper describes uncertainty quantification for molecular property predictions and separates aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit model version, calibration, uncertainty interval, applicability-domain check, and source support

disconnections.name: Out-of-domain prediction to abstention, human review, and evidence-bound confidence policy

forward_logic: separate a plausible model output from a source strong enough to guide route choice
track distance to training domain, confidence calibration, uncertainty attribution, abstention threshold, and human/source review
turn uncertain model outputs into review prompts rather than proposal generators
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat OOD predictions as review worklist items unless uncertainty and source evidence justify promotion.

evidence.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics paper discusses explainable uncertainty quantification for molecular property predictions.
Scientific Reports article notes that uncertainty quantification in molecular machine learning lacks standard general guidelines.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: low unless OOD status, abstention threshold, uncertainty attribution, and human review are explicit

disconnections.name: Route operation to DoE design space plus critical-parameter, sensitivity, and robustness boundary

break_bonds: single successful condition to design-space boundary
route step to critical-parameter sensitivity boundary
forward_logic: separate a route that worked once from a route with a known operating window
track quality attributes, critical material attributes, critical process parameters, DoE model, sensitivity, and design-space limits
avoid promoting fragile one-condition sources as robust route priors
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward route sources with explicit DoE or robustness evidence over single-condition precedents.

evidence.citation: ICH Q8(R2) describes pharmaceutical development concepts including critical quality attributes, process parameters, and design space.
ICH Q9(R1) provides quality risk management principles relevant to risk-based robustness decisions.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit CQA/CPP map, DoE model, sensitivity, design space, and validation evidence

disconnections.name: Route step to impurity response surface, failure mode, edge-of-failure, and operating-window policy

forward_logic: separate nominal success from how impurities and failures respond to parameter drift
track impurity response surfaces, failure thresholds, material variability, analytical method, and mitigation plan
flag route sources that lack any evidence near the edge of the operating window
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use failure-mode and impurity-response records when robustness, not formal reaction type, determines route quality.

evidence.citation: Chemical reaction optimization review discusses modern optimization, HTE, process scale-up, and reaction robustness concepts.
Predictive chemistry review discusses reaction development, experimental feedback, and high-throughput reaction data.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit impurity response, failure threshold, material variability, analytical method, and mitigation

disconnections.name: Benchmark route/source to analogue-series and scaffold split leakage boundary

break_bonds: analogue series to train/test leakage boundary
forward_logic: separate benchmark performance from the split lineage that makes it trustworthy
track scaffold overlap, analogue-series overlap, activity cliffs, chronological order, duplicate structures, and split seeds
avoid treating random-split performance as evidence of route generalization
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank benchmark source claims when analogue-series or scaffold leakage is not audited.

evidence.citation: Molecular representation analysis argues scaffold split is a more challenging and realistic evaluation than random split for new chemistry.
Systematic molecular-property study discusses split variability, scaffold generalization, and activity cliff challenges.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit scaffold/series groups, chronological or leakage-aware split, duplicate checks, and split manifest

disconnections.name: Reaction/template benchmark to patent-family, source-document, duplicate-template, and procedure-leakage policy

forward_logic: separate model evidence from hidden overlap between train and test reaction sources
track patent family, source document, reaction template, procedure text, duplicate row, and source extraction lineage
flag models whose route proposals may reproduce near-duplicate patent or template records from training
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Require source-document and template leakage manifests before using benchmark gains as route-source evidence.

evidence.citation: Predictive chemistry review notes that reaction-model performance can be overoptimistic without scaffold or source-document splits and can suffer from lack of negative data.
DataSAIL paper discusses similarity-induced information leakage and leakage-avoiding data splitting.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit patent-family, source-document, template, duplicate, and procedure-leakage audit

disconnections.name: Local PPTX/doc route source to manually verified route card plus structures, stereochemistry, and file-provenance boundary

break_bonds: local slide scheme to validated route-card boundary
forward_logic: separate local source extraction from a route card that can guide proposals
track source file, slide/scheme location, extracted text, manually assigned structures, stereochemistry, hazards, process notes, and reviewer signoff
avoid creating templates from local schemes until structures and stereochemistry are manually verified
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use local PPTX routes as evidence only after route-card structure and stereochemistry signoff.

evidence.citation: Local statin route extraction records PPTX-derived text/table context and embedded scheme limitations.
Local integration notes require extracting/redrawing schemes, assigning structures, checking atom mapping/stereochemistry, and tagging hazards before template promotion.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: low until local file, scheme, structures, stereochemistry, hazards, and reviewer signoff are explicit

disconnections.name: Local route card to template-promotion quarantine plus reviewer signoff and source-license policy

break_bonds: reviewed route card to executable-template boundary
local evidence to source-license and quarantine boundary
forward_logic: separate a reviewed local route card from an executable proposal source
track source permissions, template abstraction, reviewer, hazard/process context, negative controls, and quarantine/promotion status
keep local route cards advisory unless promotion requirements and source rights are explicit
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not promote local route cards into templates until source rights, abstraction, and reviewer signoff are recorded.

evidence.citation: Strategic disconnection README states these records are advisory, not ordinary templates or stock records.
Open Reaction Database overview describes structured reaction data, open access, and schema-driven reaction data goals.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: none until source rights, reviewer signoff, template abstraction, hazard context, and quarantine status are explicit

disconnections.name: False stock closure to product-like terminal artifact plus source-backed correction and guardrail boundary

break_bonds: failure trace to corrected negative-label boundary
forward_logic: separate stock closure from evidence that the route made real strategic progress
track product-like terminal similarity, advanced-intermediate status, expected strategic move, source-backed correction, and replay/test evidence
convert false closures into negative source records and guardrail labels
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Penalize stock closures that end at product-like analogues without exposing the expected strategic disconnection.

evidence.citation: Integration notes document the deacetylbufotalin failure: a product-like bufadienolide analogue was treated as stock instead of requiring C17-pyrone strategy.
AutoPlanner cascade report explains why strict stock closure is insufficient and product-like terminal audits are required.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: negative penalty when product-like terminal similarity is high and expected strategic disconnection is absent

disconnections.name: Large terminal/source artifact to carrier-reagent recognition, self-loop, unsupported atom-gain, and corrected-label policy

break_bonds: large terminal to carrier-reagent classification boundary
model artifact to corrected failure-label boundary
forward_logic: separate a large terminal that is a carrier/leaving scaffold from a product-like advanced intermediate
track atom provenance, contributed fragment, repeated/self-loop candidates, unsupported atom gains, and corrected audit label
use corrected artifact cases as hard negatives for reranking and proposal gating
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not classify large terminals by size alone; require atom-provenance and carrier-reagent context.

risks: carrier reagent mistaken for product-like terminal

evidence.citation: AutoPlanner cascade progress report records carrier reagent recognition for a Wittig phosphorane that should not be treated as product-like terminal.
Negative chemical data paper discusses the role of failed experiments and negative data in improving chemistry machine-learning models.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: negative penalty for self loops, unsupported atom gains, or unreviewed product-like terminal labels; neutralize large carrier reagents when atom provenance supports it

source_notes.summary: The v20 expansion promotes backlog families covering route decision provenance, source-conflict resolution, scale-up/technology-transfer boundaries, model uncertainty, route robustness/DoE, leakage-aware data splits, local route-card manual validation, and strategic failure-case source records.

V20 records are advisory source-policy records. Promotion requires explicit reviewer evidence and must not convert local files, model predictions, failed traces, or source-conflict records into executable reaction templates, stock closures, or validated process routes by default.
